problem_interpretation: Design a planar two-layer antireflection coating on a semi-infinite glass substrate (refractive index 1.52, lossless) with air incidence (refractive index 1.0). The stack must consist of exactly one layer of SiO2 (n=1.46) and one layer of TiO2 (n=2.40) in either order, with each layer thickness constrained between 40 and 160 nm. The objective is to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence over the wavelength range 450 to 700 nm (sampled every 5 nm). A mean reflectance below 0.03 is a stated soft target preference. The method must use deterministic Transfer Matrix Method only, excluding RCWA, FDFD, learned surrogates, or hardware acceleration. The optimization allows at most two research rounds with one route and up to 64 solver evaluations per round using seed 17. Final validation requires observing the full spectrum and performing an independent numeric check before claiming the target is met.

Use seed 17 for the optimizer. Allow a maximum of 64 solver evaluations per round. Report the best candidate's layer order, thicknesses, full reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Do not claim the target (<0.03) is met without verifying the computed mean against the reported spectrum.

The stack must consist of exactly one layer of SiO2 (n=1.46) and one layer of TiO2 (n=2.40) in either order, with each layer thickness constrained between 40 and 160 nm. The objective is to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence over the wavelength range 450 to 700 nm (sampled every 5 nm). A mean reflectance below 0.03 is a stated soft target preference. The method must use deterministic Transfer Matrix Method only, excluding RCWA, FDFD, learned surrogates, or hardware acceleration. The optimization allows at most two research rounds with one route and up to 64 solver evaluations per round using seed 17. Final validation requires observing the full spectrum and performing an independent numeric check before claiming the target is met.
